0|03668b3ceb0c7a95e09f1b6169f5270ffc1a19f6|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"oom: avoid oom killer for lowmem allocations
If memory has been depleted in lowmem zones even with the protection
afforded to it by /proc/sys/vm/lowmem_reserve_ratio
killing current users will help.  The memory is either reclaimable (or
migratable) already
column2: in which case we should not invoke the oom killer at

column1: all
column2: or it is pinned by an application for I/O.  Killing such an

column1: application may leave the hardware in an unspecified state and there is no
guarantee that it will be able to make a timely exit.
Lowmem allocations are now failed in oom conditions when __GFP_NOFAIL is
not used so that the task can perhaps recover or try again later.
Previously
column2: the heuristic provided some protection for those tasks with

column1: CAP_SYS_RAWIO
column2: but this is no longer necessary since we will not be

column1: killing tasks for the purposes of ISA allocations.
high_zoneidx is gfp_zone(gfp_flags)
column2: meaning that ZONE_NORMAL will be the

column1: default for all allocations that are not __GFP_DMA
__GFP_HIGHMEM
column2: and __GFP_MOVABLE on kernels configured to support those

column1: flags.  Testing for high_zoneidx being less than ZONE_NORMAL will only
return true for allocations that have either __GFP_DMA or __GFP_DMA32.
